title: How to Harlem Shake in 2021 | Dance Tutorial

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The instructor uses an energetic, conversational approach, demonstrating steps with continuous self-encouragement and music background. He breaks down movements section by section with verbal counting and physical cues.

lesson_structure.note: Instructor enters jumping into the frame.
Demonstration of the Harlem Shake to music.
Detailed instruction on shoulder movement and looseness.
Practicing shoulder movements with counts and hip incorporation.
Dancing to the beat with music playing.

common_mistakes: Being too stiff and trying to lock up instead of staying loose

steps_taught.name: Harlem Shake Shoulders
steps_taught.description: Alternating shoulder pops with loose body posture and hip opposition.

what_works: Clear demonstration of shoulder isolation and body looseness
what_hinders: Quick transitions between talking and demonstrating without formal counts

quotes.text: The most important thing when doing a Harlem shake, ladies and gentlemen, is the shoulders, man.
Don't be tight. Don't try to... No, it's none of that.
It's called a shake for a reason. It's not called a Harlem step.

evidence_segments.observation: Instructor stands facing front explaining shoulder movement using his hands to point to the right and left shoulders.

extraction.distinctive_method: Emphasizing the mental cue of staying loose and comparing shoulders to a key and lock mechanism.
